sections.title: Expressing quantity
sections.content:
Advanced ways to talk about amounts:
• ample — more than enough. There is ample evidence to support the claim.
• scarce — insufficient in quantity. Clean water is scarce in many regions.
• negligible — so small as to be unimportant. The difference in price was negligible.
• substantial — large in amount or importance. She made a substantial contribution to the project.
• excessive — more than necessary or reasonable. Excessive screen time can affect sleep quality.

sections.title: Degree and intensity
sections.content:
Words expressing how much or how strongly:
• utterly — completely and totally. The plan was utterly impossible.
• moderately — to a medium extent. The restaurant is moderately priced.
• marginally — by a very small amount. Sales were marginally higher than last quarter.
• predominantly — mainly, for the most part. The audience was predominantly young people.
• considerably — by a notably large amount. Prices have risen considerably this year.

exercises.question: An amount so small it's not worth considering is:
exercises.explanation: Negligible means too small or unimportant to be worth considering.

exercises.question: When resources are insufficient, they are:
exercises.explanation: Scarce means insufficient for the demand; in short supply.

exercises.question: A large and meaningful amount is:
exercises.explanation: Substantial means of considerable importance, size, or worth.

exercises.question: 'Marginally' means by:
exercises.explanation: Marginally means to only a limited extent; slightly.

exercises.question: More than necessary or reasonable is:
exercises.explanation: Excessive means more than is necessary, normal, or desirable.

exercises.question: 'Predominantly' means:
exercises.explanation: Predominantly means mainly; for the most part.

exercises.question: Having more than enough of something is having:
exercises.explanation: Ample means enough or more than enough; plentiful.
